results.name: Azrar
results.description:
**Kabyle Traditional Necklace-
Azrar**
This 3D model represents a traditional Kabyle necklace inspired by Amazigh (Berber) jewelry from northern Algeria. The necklace is composed of natural-style red coral beads arranged along the strand, separated by small silver spacers that add rhythm and balance to the design.

At the center hangs a circular pendant crafted in an aged silver style, richly decorated with colorful enamel motifs in green, blue, and yellow. A polished red coral cabochon sits at the heart of the pendant, surrounded by fine beadwork and floral patterns typical of Kabyle ornamentation. Delicate dangling elements extend from the lower edge of the pendant, enhancing movement and visual richness.

The combination of coral, enamel, and textured silver gives the piece an authentic handcrafted appearance, ideal for cultural heritage visualization, jewelry showcases, historical assets, games, and cinematic projects.

results.name: Large Effigy Brazier
results.description:
Anthropomorphic incense burner representing a standing male figure wearing a bird mask with round eye sockets, an open beak, and horn-like projections on the upper section. The figure stands with legs apart and arms bent: the left hand rests on the abdomen, while the right hand is raised holding a club. On the posterior side, behind the figure, is the vessel that serves as the incense container, supported by a cylindrical stand. The entire assemblage rests on a pedestal base decorated with conical elements in relief. The figure wears a necklace, circular earspools, a loincloth, and a chest covering resembling a net composed of tubular and circular beads.
 IDAEH Cultural Property No. 1.2.144.0875
www.fundacionrutamaya.org

Special thanks to the staff of La Ruta Maya Foundation for their hard work on this project.

results.name: Mosaic Neptune-Amphitrite - HERCULANEUM | ITALY
results.description:
Mosaic of Neptune and Amphitrite

Neptune, the god of the sea, is recognizable by his trident, his wild beard, flowing locks, and blue mantle, while Amphitrite (in Latin as Salacia), semi-nude, appears as the queen of the sea, adorned with a diadem, necklace, arm band, and earrings. Neptune fell in love with Amphitrite, but she initially fled him. With the help of Delphinus, the dolphin, Neptune found her. Delphinus was rewarded by being turned into a constellation, and Amphitrite became the goddess of the sea. Even though the artist was working with small stones, he still artfully conveyed Neptune’s musculature and Amphitrite’s shapely curves. In both cases, the drapery responds to the shape of their bodies. He stands in a contrapposto pose, suggesting a sculpture of a god or athlete might have been the source for his pose, while she leans against a pillar, indicating that the inspiration for this mosaic was a statue , perhaps, one of Venus.

results.name: Vaso/Vase - Tholos of Santiago do Escoural
results.description:
The Tholos of Santiago do Escoural was discovered in early August 1964 by coal workers at the Herdade da Sala, in an area proximate to the western side of the Escoural Cave (Gruta do Escoural). In early September of the same year, archaeologist Manuel Farinha dos Santos carried out an excavation which led to the discovery of a large amount of funerary remains (schist slabs, necklace beads and arrowheads).
Among the objects recovered in the excavation, this vase stands out, not only because it is intact, but also due to the symbolic decoration it presents. The type of decoration this vase has, although rather schematic, represents the same theme as other votive and ceremonial objects from the same period. In the most well-preserved depictions on schist slabs, cyllindrical idols, or pottery from this period, representations of human faces are easily identified, thus referring to the world of magic/religion.
Original scan by Global Digital Heritage in 2019 and optimized with Myou Software decimator.
